transcript.text: I reviewed the county health guidance for the pantry this week, and there are some requirements our draft plan doesn't currently reflect. The guidance specifies that refrigerated food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or colder, with the temperature logged every 2 hours while the pantry is open — our draft only proposes a weekly temperature check, which won't be sufficient. The guidance also requires sealed packages to display allergen labels, which goes beyond our current plan's reference to the district's standard food-labeling procedure. I have the printed guidance in my health-office binder and I'd like to make sure these requirements are incorporated into the final plan.

transcript.text: Thank you both for those critical findings. Nurse Rivera, the health and safety updates are clear — we'll need to revise the temperature logging to every 2 hours during pantry hours and set the refrigeration standard at 41 degrees or colder, plus incorporate the allergen labeling requirement beyond our district's standard procedure. Mr. Hassan, the family outreach results are equally important — we'll need to shift pickup to Thursday evenings from 5:00 to 7:00 p.m. and add Somali to our intake materials alongside English and Spanish. I'd like to ask a couple of clarifying questions before we finalize. Nurse Rivera, does the county guidance specify anything about how the temperature logs should be documented or stored? And Mr. Hassan, do we have the capacity to get Somali translations completed before next month's opening, or do we need to identify a translator resource?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Thank you, Ms. Brooks. To your first question — the county guidance specifies that the temperature must be logged every 2 hours while the pantry is open, but it doesn't go into detail about a specific format for the log itself. I'd recommend we use a simple log sheet kept near the refrigerator that records the date, time, temperature reading, and the initials of whoever takes the reading. That's a standard approach I've seen work well in other settings. I can draft a template for that and bring it to our next check-in. As for the allergen labeling requirement, I want to flag that we'll need to think through how that works in practice — the guidance requires sealed packages to display allergen labels, so we'll need to make sure any food we accept or distribute meets that standard before it goes on the shelves. I'm happy to work with whoever is handling food sourcing to make sure that's built into our intake process.
